messages.subject: Survey design
parts:
Hi All,

two days back at work after workshop last week and have a new distance project on my desk already!

The field survey team have designed new survey with the intention of sampling on just one side of the transect line (due to issues of surface glare making detecting seabirds on surface difficult).  I've said to include both sides, mainly to reduce risk of getting a small sample size, and we can then include a proxy for surface glare as a covariate when we run Distance.  Are there any other specific pitfalls / considerations to take into account if sampling on one side only - just seems wrong to me!!? I don't think that there will be issues with increased uncertainty when extrapolating to a larger area, as study is based on 2 visits, each visit comprising 25x transects, 6km long, 1km apart, within a study area of 6x25km. 

Thanks!

messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Survey design
parts:
Colin

Happy to know you're back at your desk, complete with a new sampling project.

The topic of one-sided transects is something we did not discuss last week, but there is a figure on p. 118 in the introductory notes we provided to you


I agree with you exhorting the crew to exert effort on both sides and cope with glare (or side) perhaps as a covariate.  The difficulty with one-sided transects is the influence of uncertainty regarding whether an animal is just outside the strip (meaning it is not recorded) or just inside the strip (meaning it enters the data with a very small perpendicular distance).  The propensity of observers is to record detections, hence the potential exists to (as the slide notes) create a spike at zero distance.  As you learned last week, from watching Len work with the blue monkey dataset, fitting a detection to data with a spike at zero distance is not pleasant.
